requirement: If every `vet_answer` callback invoked by {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.vet_answer` returns `Ok(VetResult::Accept)`, or the request has no callbacks, the answer is successfully submitted and the agent conversation ends.
rationale:
**Obligations in `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.vet_answer.ok`:** (a) when every callback returns `Ok(Accept)`, the answer is submitted successfully; (b) when the request has no callbacks, the answer is submitted successfully; (c) in both cases the agent conversation ends.

**Callbacks that all accept.** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[vetting_collects_corrections_and_rechecks_every_callback]` registers three callbacks. In the first round the scripted answer is `false`. The second callback corrects, and the third also corrects because it runs while its flag is still set. In the second round the answer is `true`, and all three callbacks return `Accept`. The test asserts these outcomes:
- `.await.unwrap()` yields `true`, so the submission succeeds.
- `seen == [false, true]` shows that the first callback ran on every submission.
- `requests.len() == 2` shows that no further request was made after the all-accept round, so the conversation ended. The script holds exactly two turns, so another turn would have failed.

**No callbacks.** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[one_submission_accepts_only_its_value_and_skips_other_calls_and_prose]` calls `ctx.ask::<bool>()` with no `vet_answer` callback. It asserts that the awaited result is `Ok(false)`, which is the submitted value. It also asserts that exactly one request was made, so the conversation ended after the first submission.

Both tests carry a `{test}` reference to the subject. The callback error, correction and ordering behaviour belongs to `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.vet_answer` and `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.vet_answer.corrections`, not to this subject. I found no gap.
